findings.title: Validation can be bypassed via DNS rebinding between resolution and the actual request
findings.evidence: The code validates the hostname with a separate DNS lookup, then performs a fresh requests.get by hostname, so the connection can be made to a different IP than the one that was checked if DNS changes between those two steps.
findings.recommendation: Bind the outbound connection to the validated address set instead of re-resolving in requests, or use a transport/adapter that resolves once, verifies the chosen IP is allowed, and connects to that exact IP while preserving TLS hostname verification.

findings.title: Address-family assumptions make allowlisted hosts fail when getaddrinfo returns non-IP entries
findings.evidence: The loop unconditionally passes the first sockaddr element to ip_address, but getaddrinfo can return entries for unsupported families where info[4][0] is not a plain IPv4 or IPv6 literal, causing a ValueError and aborting fetches for otherwise valid hosts.
findings.recommendation: Filter getaddrinfo results to AF_INET and AF_INET6 before calling ip_address, or catch ValueError per entry and ignore unsupported address families while still requiring at least one valid public IP result.
